title: Mathematical Foundations
text: DGGRID defines three orientation classes based child cells align parent cells subdivision: Class : Child cell vertices align parent cell vertices. Hexagons “flat top” orientation. Class II: Child cell centers align parent cell vertices. Hexagons rotated 30° (“pointy top”). Class III: Neither alignment—child cells rotated relative parent cells (skewed grids). aperture produces characteristic class pattern: aperture 3, odd resolutions (1, 3, 5, …) produce Class grids flat-top hexagons, even resolutions (2, 4, 6, …) produce Class II grids pointy-top hexagons. aperture 4, 2×2 subdivision preserves alignment, resolutions Class . aperture 7, subdivision involves √7 scaling arctan(√3/5) rotation, creating characteristic Class III skewed pattern. rotation accumulates: resolution 2 rotated 2×arctan(√3/5) resolution 0, . mixed aperture (4/3), class pattern follows aperture 4 (Class ) first m levels, switches aperture 3’s alternating /II pattern subsequent levels. class affects hexagon orientation coordinate system internals, fundamental cell assignment equal-area property.

title: Mathematical Foundations
text: aperture 3, Z3 curve uses base-3 (ternary) encoding. resolution level adds one ternary digit representing 3 child cells contains point. three child positions form triangular arrangement within parent cell. digit values correspond : 0: Center-bottom child 1: Upper-left child 2: Upper-right child encoding preserves hierarchy: truncating last digit gives parent cell index.

title: Mathematical Foundations
text: aperture 4, Morton curve (Z-order curve) interleaves bits j grid coordinates. classic space-filling curve maps 2D grid 1D index preserving locality. 2×2 subdivision level creates 4 child cells arranged square: child position encoded 2 bits: low bit , high bit j. resolution r, index uses 2r bits total. interleaving creates characteristic “Z” pattern gives curve name.
code: +---+---+   | 2 | 3 |   +---+---+   | 0 | 1 |   +---+---+ For cell at grid position (i, j):   bit 0 = i₀, bit 1 = j₀   (resolution 1)   bit 2 = i₁, bit 3 = j₁   (resolution 2)   ... # Z-order index idx4 <- hexify_lonlat_to_index(16.37, 48.21, resolution = 5, aperture = 4) cat("Z-order index:", idx4, "\n") #> Z-order index: 0233232  # The index encodes (quad, i, j) implicitly coords <- hexify_index_to_cell(idx4, aperture = 4) cat("Decoded - Quad:", coords$quad, "i:", coords$i, "j:", coords$j, "\n") #> Decoded - Quad: i: 31 j: 26

title: Mathematical Foundations
text: Aperture 7 uses base-7 encoding twist: subdivision involves scaling √7 rotation arctan(√3/5). 7 child cells form hexagonal rosette pattern: center cell (0) surrounded 6 peripheral cells (1-6) arranged hexagonal ring. Unlike apertures 3 4, child cells rotated relative parent, aperture 7 produces Class III grids. encoding uses Eisenstein integers (complex numbers form + bω ω = e^(2πi/3)) handle hexagonal geometry. digit 0-6 represents position rosette.

title: Hexify Complete Rewrite Plan
text: Create GLOSSARY.md :
code: # DGGS Terminology  ## Coordinate Systems  ### PROJTRI (Projected Triangle) - `(triangle_index, triangle_x, triangle_y)` - Output of Snyder forward projection - triangle_index: 0-19 (icosahedron faces) - triangle_x, triangle_y: normalized [0,1] within face  ### Q2DD (Quad 2D Double) - `(quad_index, x, y)` with floating-point x,y - Intermediate representation after triangle-to-quad conversion - quad_index: 0-11 (pairs of triangles forming rhombuses)  ### Q2DI (Quad 2D Integer) - `(quad_index, cell_i, cell_j)` with integer indices - Final cell identification at a given resolution - Used by DGGRID for cell assignment  ### SEQNUM (Sequential Number) - Single integer uniquely identifying each cell globally - Formula: `face * cells_per_face + local_index` - Useful for database storage and indexing  ## Projection Terms  ### Snyder Projection Equal-area projection from sphere to icosahedron faces. - Forward: (lon, lat) → (triangle_index, triangle_x, triangle_y) - Inverse: (triangle_index, triangle_x, triangle_y) → (lon, lat)  ### Face Azimuth Offset Per-face rotation angle to align projection with icosahedron orientation. Variable: `face_azimuth_offset` (previously `dazh`)  ## Grid Terms  ### Aperture Ratio of cell areas between successive resolution levels. - Aperture 3: Each parent contains ~3 children (1:√3 linear scale) - Aperture 4: Each parent contains 4 children (1:2 linear scale) - Aperture 7: Each parent contains ~7 children (1:√7 linear scale)  ### Rotation Class Orientation of hexagons at each resolution level. - Class 1: Flat-top orientation (vertex pointing up) - Class 2: Pointy-top orientation (edge pointing up) - Class 3A/3B: Intermediate orientations (aperture 7 only)  ### Effective Resolution Resolution level accounting for aperture effects. Higher = smaller cells, more cells globally.  ### Surrogate Grid Fine-resolution grid used to approximate non-Class-1 cell positions. Used internally for Class 2 and Class 3 quantization.
